# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty — https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html

**Member:** Quinn Ellison
**Member ID:** W391580594
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-04
**Reference number:** POC-DF42BEB029-97975
**Payer/Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Montana

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my knee condition, and I believe the records support this under Aetna's own policy, CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty.

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I have reviewed the plan's published criteria for knee arthroplasty, and I believe my medical records meet them.

**1. The affected compartment**

Aetna's policy states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-05-28 shows full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition limited to the medial compartment, with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. No other compartment is described as affected. This is consistent with the single-compartment disease that the plan's own criteria identify as the basis for a unicompartmental procedure.

The policy also states:

> "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note ):"

My imaging findings — advanced (grade 4), single-compartment osteoarthritis of the medial compartment — match this description.

**2. Conservative therapy**

Aetna's policy states:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My records show I completed 16 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (24 visits, from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17), which is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 12-week minimum described above, and all of it was formal, in-person therapy — not home-based or virtual care. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-02, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. Despite this sustained course of treatment, I continue to have pain that wakes me 3-4 times a night and prevents me from climbing stairs without assistance.

**3. Timing of the corticosteroid injection**

I understand the policy identifies a contraindication when a corticosteroid injection occurs:

> "or Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty;"

My injection was given on 2026-05-02. Based on the timeline of my care, I believe this falls outside the 12-week window relative to the planned procedure, but I am including this date so that the reviewer can confirm the interval against the planned surgical date of [insert planned surgery date, if not already in the chart].

**Summary**

Taken together, the MRI findings, the documented single-compartment disease, and the extent of conservative treatment I have completed appear to align with the plan's own published criteria for medically necessary unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. I am asking that Aetna reconsider the denial in light of this information and the complete medical record submitted by my surgeon.

**Deadline and submission**

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31 (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available through my account at aetna.com, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379. I will also confirm the correct appeal address printed on my denial letter before sending.

Thank you for reviewing my appeal. Please let me know if any additional records are needed from me or from Dr. Lindqvist's office.

Sincerely,

[Quinn Ellison]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W391580594

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
